title: 'VisionQuest' Takes a Side in a Big 'WandaVision' Debate
summary:
Marvel's newest Disney+ series, 'VisionQuest,' is weighing in on an argument fans have had since 2021. Warning: this story includes spoilers for Episode 3.

'VisionQuest' continues the story that began in 'WandaVision' and continued in 'Agatha All Along.' It follows Vision, an android hero played by Paul Bettany, and his son Tommy, played by Ruaridh Mollica.

In 'WandaVision,' viewers learned that the TV-sitcom world in the town of Westview, New Jersey, was created by Wanda with a magic spell. She was deeply sad after losing Vision and used her powers to build a pretend life. But that meant controlling the people of the whole town. Some fans saw Wanda as a villain in the making. Others saw her as a hero who was overwhelmed by grief and did not mean to cause harm.

In Episode 3, called 'Reboot,' Vision tries to explain to Tommy where he came from. He describes the spell, how Wanda created her sons Tommy and Billy, and calls her actions morally wrong. The writer of the original article says some fans may be upset by this.

This Vision is not exactly the same one from 'WandaVision.' He is known as White Vision, rebuilt from the original Vision's parts. He shares the original's love for Wanda but is less ruled by his feelings.

The writer thinks the show is not simply calling Wanda a villain. It admits her actions hurt people, while treating the creation of Tommy as something good. The writer hopes showrunner Terry Matalas can fix what they see as a weak ending to 'WandaVision.'

New episodes stream on Disney+ every Tuesday.
why_it_matters: The episode shows how a story can admit a character caused harm without calling her simply a villain, which keeps an old fan debate going.

background_read: The Marvel Cinematic Universe is a large group of connected superhero movies and TV shows.
Several Marvel series on Disney+ continue stories from one another, so characters and events carry over.
Fans often debate whether a character is a hero or a villain, especially when a character does harm while feeling great sadness.
Episodes of many streaming shows are released once a week, and articles warn readers about spoilers before discussing them.
